body:
There is an existing [Python proposal](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-python/issues/1502), this is basically the same one but for the go sdk. The high-level approach is similar to the Python proposal (mirror the existing aws implementation, introduced in this **[PR](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-go/pull/2257)).** Also, I'd be happy to do the implementation PRs and help maintaining once we agree on the high-level approach.

To re-iterate I was thinking:

- Keep a similar wrapper (module) of the actual google sdk like the [aws driver does](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-go/tree/main/contrib/aws/s3driver/awssdkv2), to avoid pulling in the google storage dependency if one wants to implement a custom storage driver. The interface will be defined like the [AWS one](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-go/blob/main/contrib/aws/s3driver/client.go), though note that methods may differ due to differences between vendors (I think this is acceptable, but let me know if you think otherwise)
- The actual driver implementation would probably be more or less as the [existing](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-go/blob/main/contrib/aws/s3driver/driver.go) driver code, since the only thing that really is different is the interaction with the cloud provider

I did start the driver implementation [here](https://github.com/Ozoniuss/sdk-go/tree/ozoniuss.gcp-driver/contrib/gcp/storagedriver) to understand how it would look like and what the differences were compared to the AWS sdk and I also wanted to experiment a bit with integration tests against a real bucket. Would like to clarify some details before moving forward:

- I did use the [fake-gcs-server](https://github.com/fsouza/fake-gcs-server) for a fake GCS implementation though let me know if you have another preference. Honestly, I've never used a package for mocking external storage before and this seemed to be the most popular. But I did write the tests such that they work with a real bucket as well. See [my implementation](https://github.com/Ozoniuss/sdk-go/blob/ozoniuss.gcp-driver/contrib/gcp/storagedriver/gcpsdk/client_test.go) for more details. I kept it since I was going to test against the real thing anyway and realized I could do it with minimal test structure changes. I think it's probably not worth setting up automated tests against a real bucket, but found it to be a useful addition for me while developing locally. Note that unless the integration tests are configured to run, only the tests against the fake will be picked up.
- There will probably be a lot of duplication in the actual driver implementation (for aws, [driver.go](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-go/blob/main/contrib/aws/s3driver/driver.go)). How would you prefer to handle this? I think for two drivers code duplication is not too bad, and will also be future-proof in case the client interfaces will diverge in the future between vendors. Though at the same time I also think it may end up being harder to maintain if more drivers are added. I was thinking one approach to handle this duplication could be to extend [ExternalStorage](https://github.com/Ozoniuss/sdk-go/blob/ozoniuss.gcp-driver/internal/extstore/extstore.go#L4) with potentially shared functionality -- for example, `extstore.ExternalStorage` may be configurable to use a custom function for building the object key, which is currently fully handled by the driver. Though, I haven't really explored the code much to understand what changes this would require -- can come back with more thoughts later.

There are some minor differences in terms of the GCS sdk compared to the AWS one but I think it's probably best to discuss those on the actual PR?

Thanks!
title: Proposal: Google Cloud Storage external storage driver in contrib (mirror of aws/s3driver)
